claim: San Diego Zoo 2026 gate price is $78 adult (12+) and $68 child (3-11), discountable to $70/$60 online; admission includes Skyfari Aerial Tram, Guided Bus Tour, and all shows.
quote: gate price for 1-Day passes is $78 for adults (ages 12+) and $68 for children (ages 3-11)... Park entry, Skyfari Aerial Tram, Guided Bus tour, All regularly scheduled shows

claim: Beginning in 2026 the San Diego Zoo charges $16 per vehicle per day for parking ($44 for oversized vehicles); the zoo is at 2920 Zoo Drive.
quote: $16 per vehicle, per day, for automobiles and motorcycles. Oversized vehicles are $44 per vehicle per day.

claim: The Balboa Park Explorer Pass costs $75 adult / $50 youth for the 7-day Parkwide (16 museums), $63 adult / $41 youth for the 1-day Limited (up to 4 museums), and starts at $109 for the annual pass.
quote: Parkwide Pass: Adults (age 12+): $75, Youth (age 3-11): $50; Limited Pass: Adults: $63, Youth: $41; Annual Pass: Starting at $109

claim: The Balboa Park Explorer Pass covers 16 participating museums and includes one Fleet Science Center IMAX dome film, but excludes the San Diego Zoo and performing-arts venues.
quote: All pass types include one documentary film at the Fleet Science Center's IMAX dome theater... do not include the San Diego Zoo, San Diego Zoo Safari Park, Comic-Con Museum, or any of the performing arts venues

claim: USS Midway Museum 2026 admission is $39 online ($41 at door) for adults 13+, $29/$31 for youth 4-12, $26 for veterans, free for children under 3 and active-duty military; includes a self-guided audio tour.
quote: Adults (13+): $39 online / $41 at door; Youth (4-12): $29 online / $31 at door; Veterans (with ID): $26; Children 3 and under: Free; Active-Duty Military & Reservists: Free

claim: Cabrillo National Monument 2026 entrance fees are $20 per private vehicle, $15 per motorcycle, and $10 per individual on foot or bicycle, each valid for 7 days; children 15 and under are free.
quote: Private Vehicle: $20.00... Motorcycle: $15.00... Individual (foot/bicycle): $10.00 per person... Children 15 and under: Free

claim: Cabrillo National Monument is generally open daily 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, offering Point Loma panoramas, the Old Point Loma Lighthouse, and tidepools.
quote: The park is generally open daily from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

claim: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park is free to enter, with five original adobe buildings, free daily ranger tours at 11am and 2pm, a working blacksmith, mariachi and Ballet Folklorico performances, and 4-hour free parking.
quote: Admission to the Old Town State Historic Park and the individual museums is free of charge... Five original adobe buildings... Excellent free park tours are offered daily at 11am & 2pm

claim: The Gaslamp Quarter holds the largest collection of commercial Victorian-style buildings in the U.S. — nearly 100 historic buildings across 16.5 walkable blocks — with 100+ restaurants, bars and nightclubs, the Davis-Horton House museum, the 1990 archway sign, and adjacency to Petco Park.
quote: nearly 100 historical building in the 16.5 walkable blocks... Davis-Horton House... the iconic Gaslamp Quarter Archway Sign, installed in 1990

claim: Old Town's historic structures include Casa de Estudillo (1820s elite life) and the Robinson Rose house, which housed the visitor center; the nearby Whaley House (built 1857) is reputed San Diego's most haunted building.
quote: Casa de Estudillo which recreates the life of San Diego's elite during the 1820s, and the Robinson Rose house... The Whaley House, built by Thomas Whaley in 1857 and reputed to be the most haunted house in San Diego

claim: La Jolla Cove is best for swimming/snorkeling/seal watching as a protected marine reserve, while La Jolla Shores is best for families and beginner surfers with wide gentle sand and a large paid parking lot.
quote: La Jolla Cove ... Best for: Swimming, snorkeling, seal watching ... protected marine reserve ... La Jolla Shores ... Best for: Families, beginner surfers, kayaking ... Large paid parking lot

claim: California sea lions concentrate at La Jolla Cove/Point La Jolla while Pacific harbor seals occupy Children's Pool (Casa Beach), a NOAA rookery; Point La Jolla and Boomer Beach have been closed since Nov 2023, Children's Pool closes to swimmers Dec 15-May 15 for pupping, and visitors should keep 50 feet from the animals.
quote: Point La Jolla has been closed year-round since November 2023 ... close the beach from December 15 through May 15 so the seals can have and rear their newborn pups ... The recommended distance is 50 feet.

claim: Coronado Beach has been named to Dr. Beach's Top Ten Beaches in North America every year from 2016 to 2024 and to Travel + Leisure's 25 Best Beaches in the U.S. in 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2025.
quote: Top Ten Beaches in North America (2016-2024) ... Ranked among the 25 Best Beaches in the U.S. (2020, 2022, 2024, 2025)

claim: Sunset Cliffs is San Diego's premier sunset-viewing spot with rugged sandstone cliffs and is a legendary surf break, while Ocean Beach is the most beginner-friendly surf area with room to spread between peaks.
quote: Sunset Cliffs is the most popular viewing spot to watch the sunset ... Ocean Beach beach breaks are the place to go, as this area is the most newcomer friendly

claim: Torrey Pines parking is about $20 per vehicle (more on weekends/holidays), the reserve is open daily 7am to sunset, and key trails include the easy 0.7-mile Guy Fleming loop, 1.3-mile Razor Point, and 0.75-mile Beach Trail down to the sand.
quote: $20 per vehicle (varies on weekends and holidays)... Open daily from 7 a.m. to sunset... Guy Fleming Trail: 0.7 miles (loop) | Easy... Razor Point Trail: 1.3 miles (round-trip)... Beach Trail: 0.75 miles (one-way) | Moderate to difficult

claim: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve uses demand-based day-use parking of roughly $15-$25 per vehicle, with free public parking available near the trailheads at the Extension and acceptance of the California State Parks annual day-use pass.
quote: The general admission day use fee is $15-$25 per vehicle with demand-based pricing, or you can use a valid annual California State Parks Vehicle Day Use Pass. Free public parking is allowed near the trail heads at the Extension.

claim: La Jolla Kayak's guided sea-cave tour runs 90-120 minutes through the Ecological Reserve, departing daily from 9am to sunset (weather permitting), and includes helmet, PFD, paddle instruction, and wildlife like leopard sharks, Garibaldi, sea lions and occasional dolphins.
quote: 90-120 minutes give or take for the whole experience... Departs throughout the day starting at 9 AM (weather permitting)... leopard sharks, Garibaldi (California's state marine fish!), lush kelp beds, sea lions, and even the occasional pod of dolphins.

claim: La Jolla sea-cave kayak tours run daily year-round and start around $64 per kayak, with most tours lasting 90 minutes to 2 hours and tandem kayaks priced roughly $74-$119 depending on operator and season.
quote: Tours start at $64 per kayak... most tours last 90 minutes to 2 hours, with prices ranging from $74-$119 for tandem kayaks and $84 for single kayaks, depending on the operator and season.

claim: San Diego has two whale-watching seasons: roughly December-April when about 20,000 gray whales migrate past (peak January-February, mother-calf pairs March-April), and mid-June through September when blue whales feed offshore.
quote: December through April, when approximately 20,000 gray whales migrate past San Diego's coast, and June through September, when blue whales feed on dense krill concentrations offshore... Blue whales are often seen off the coast of San Diego from mid-June through September.

claim: Gray-whale season tours (Dec-April) typically run 2-3 hours and cost about $35-$75, while summer blue-whale tours are longer and can run roughly $190-$325 per person, though budget options can be found for $20-$30.
quote: Gray whale tours (Dec-April) are shorter—2-3 hours usually, $35-$75. Blue whale season tours are longer, $190-$325 per person sometimes... as cheap as 20-30$ per person

claim: La Jolla Shores is San Diego's top beginner surf spot thanks to its gently sloping sandy bottom and semi-protected, rolling waves, while Pacific Beach's Tourmaline Surf Park and Law Street near Crystal Pier are also forgiving learner breaks.
quote: La Jolla Shores has long ranked as San Diego's top spot for upstart surfers, with its gently sloping sand, semi-protected waters and plentiful surf outfitters... the famed Tourmaline Surf Park being a haven for learners and longboarders, and Law Street Beach near Crystal Pier offering generally forgiving waves.

claim: Surf Diva, founded in 1996 in La Jolla as the first all-female surf school, offers beginner lessons at La Jolla Shores, and other major operators include Everyday California (La Jolla Shores) and Pacific Surf School (Pacific Beach).
quote: Surf Diva, founded in 1996 by twin sisters Coco and Izzy Tihanyi, is the first all-female surf school and one of the most renowned surf schools on Earth.

claim: The Point Loma tide pools at Cabrillo National Monument are the best-known and one of the best-protected rocky intertidal areas in California, best visited at negative low tides in the fall and winter months.
quote: The Point Loma tide pools, located along the shoreline of Cabrillo National Monument, are the best known in San Diego and are one of the best protected rocky intertidal areas in California.

claim: Cabrillo National Monument charges $20 per vehicle (or $10 per pedestrian/cyclist) and is open 9am-5pm with the tidepool area closing at 4:30pm, while La Jolla's natural tide pools at Shell Beach, Dike Rock and South Casa Beach are free to access.
quote: The entrance fee to Cabrillo National Monument is $20 per vehicle or $10 per pedestrian or cyclist, with children 15 and under free... Access to all of the natural tide pools in La Jolla is free... Shell Beach, Dike Rock, and South Casa Beach.

claim: The Mission Bay Bike Path offers about 12 miles of flat scenic riding past Mission Bay's parks, connecting to the roughly 3-mile Mission Beach/Pacific Beach boardwalk from Crystal Pier to the South Mission jetty.
quote: 12 miles of flat, scenic bike paths passing by all of Mission Bay's public parks... This iconic path stretches approximately 3 miles along the sandy shores, from the Crystal Pier in Pacific Beach to the jetty in South Mission Beach.

claim: The Bayshore Bikeway is a roughly 24-mile mostly flat loop around San Diego Bay connecting Coronado to downtown, with the Coronado/Silver Strand stretch offering skyline and Hotel del Coronado views; bike rentals are widely available near the Coronado ferry landing and along Mission Boulevard.
quote: The full Bayshore Bikeway loop stretches over 24 miles, connecting Coronado to downtown San Diego and the surrounding areas... The Silver Strand Bikeway is a scenic route connecting Coronado to Imperial Beach.

claim: The Michelin Guide lists exactly two starred restaurants in the city of San Diego: Soichi (1 star) and Addison (3 stars).
quote: San Diego and surroundings: 1-2 of 2 restaurants — Soichi; Addison

claim: Soichi, an intimate omakase Japanese restaurant in University Heights, is a One Star: High quality cooking entry in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide USA.
quote: Soichi is a One Star: High quality cooking restaurant in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide USA. Named for Chef Soichi Kadoya, this intimate Japanese restaurant has made a name for itself in University Heights.

claim: Addison at the Fairmont Grand Del Mar (chef William Bradley) earned its third Michelin star in 2022, the only three-star restaurant in Southern California.
quote: Addison at the Fairmont Grand Del Mar earned its third star in 2022, becoming one of just seven restaurants in the state to boast Michelin's highest honor, and the only one in Southern California.

claim: San Diego has eight Bib Gourmand restaurants: Callie, LOLA 55, Ciccia Osteria, Morning Glory, Cucina Urbana, Mabel's Gone Fishing, Cesarina, and Carmelita Molino y Cocina.
quote: San Diego and surroundings: 1-8 of 8 restaurants — Callie; LOLA 55; Ciccia Osteria; Morning Glory; Cucina Urbana; Mabel's Gone Fishing; Cesarina; Carmelita Molino y Cocina

claim: San Diego markets itself as the 'Capital of Craft' with more than 150 independent breweries and over 200 brewery-owned venues across the county.
quote: Visitors can choose from more than 150 independent breweries and over 200 brewery-owned venues scattered from the coast to the backcountry, earning San Diego the marketing nickname 'Capital of Craft.'

claim: Stone Brewing (founded 1996, with a large Escondido facility) was once a top-ten US craft brewery producing over 325,000 barrels annually before being sold to Sapporo USA for $168 million in 2022.
quote: by 2016, Stone was one of the ten largest craft breweries in the U.S., producing more than 325,000 barrels of beer annually. However, by 2022...the company was sold to Sapporo USA for $168 million.

claim: Brewery openings have slowed, averaging about eight per year from 2021-2024 with only five debuting in 2025; Modern Times was split into separate beer, coffee and hospitality entities with a North Park 'Cathedral of Caffeination' concept.
quote: an average of eight having opened each year from 2021 to 2024, and only five breweries debuting in 2025

claim: North Park anchors San Diego's brewery scene with North Park Beer Company plus outposts of Pure Project and Fall Brewing; AleSmith and Societe are standouts in Miramar/Kearny Mesa.
quote: North Park Beer Company - described as having consistently high-quality brews and 360-degree approach to hospitality; Pure Project - locations in...North Park; Fall Brewing (North Park and South Park)

claim: Barrio Logan's pioneering Latino-owned Border X Brewing (open since 2014 on Logan Avenue, a James Beard nominee) closed its Barrio Logan location in early 2025, with Mason Ale Works reviving the space as a shared tasting room.
quote: Border X Brewing Closes Its Doors In San Diego's Historic Barrio Logan After A Decade Serving The Community

claim: Little Italy is the largest Little Italy in the US at 48 square blocks, a foodie hub of Italian restaurants, delis, craft breweries and Wednesday/Saturday farmers markets, while North Park is the hipster food-and-bar scene with dive bars, art walks and music festivals.
quote: San Diego has the largest Little Italy in the U.S., at 48 square blocks...North Park is San Diego's hottest food and bar scene, with more award-winning restaurants and bars per square mile than anywhere else in the city.

claim: The Gaslamp Quarter is downtown's nightlife and entertainment hub with over 200 restaurants, nightclubs, rooftop bars and galleries, while Barrio Logan is the Mexican-American cultural district with taquerias, Chicano Park murals and art galleries on Logan Avenue.
quote: over 200 restaurants, nightclubs, galleries, and shops...Barrio Logan is known for Mexican culture and food, with the Mexican heritage reflected on Logan Avenue, from the taquerias to the small galleries to the murals in Chicano Park.

claim: SeaWorld San Diego's all-new Shark Encounter opened in 2026, and Summer Spectacular nighttime animal experiences and shows (Shamu Celebration: Light Up the Night, Dolphins: Touch the Sky, Sea Lions Tonite) run select dates May 22 through September 7, 2026.
quote: Shark Encounter - Now Open! ... Nighttime Animal Experiences launching on June 12, 2026 ... Shamu Celebration: Light Up the Night, Dolphins: Touch the Sky, and Sea Lions Tonite ... from May 22 through September 7, 2026

claim: SeaWorld San Diego single-day tickets start as low as $59.99 (regular $126.99), with All-Day Dining addable for $40/day.
quote: Single-Day SeaWorld San Diego Tickets are available for as low as $59.99, with a regular price of $126.99. All-Day Dining can be added for $40/day.

claim: Legoland California's new space-themed land LEGO Galaxy is now open, anchored by the Galacticoaster plus two more rides, character encounters, and a toddler play zone.
quote: the all-new space-themed land LEGO Galaxy ... featuring Galacticoaster ... plus two more rides, character encounters, a toddler-friendly play zone, cosmic bites, and galactic gear

claim: Legoland California single-day tickets start at $69 online (front gate $139); Resort Hopper tickets covering the theme park, SEA LIFE Aquarium and Water Park start at $69 with a Water Park FREE promotion running through June 30, 2026; children under 2 are free.
quote: Single Day Tickets - Starting price: $69 per person ... Front gate price: $139 ... Resort Hopper Tickets (3 parks) ... 'Get Water Park FREE' promotion running through June 30, 2026 ... Children under 2 receive free admission

claim: San Diego Zoo Safari Park's Denny Sanford Elephant Valley is now open for 2026, housing one of the largest elephant herds in North America; discounted admission is about $70 adult / $60 child (3-11), admission includes the Africa Tram, and non-member parking is $20.
quote: New for 2026: Denny Sanford Elephant Valley is now open at the Safari Park ... one of the largest elephant herds in North America ... Discounted ticket prices are $70 for adults and $60 for children (ages 3-11) ... Non-members pay $20 for parking.

claim: Birch Aquarium at Scripps (La Jolla) charges $34.95 adult / $29.95 child (3-12) online (walk-up $39.95/$34.95), under 3 free, opens daily at 9 a.m. with seasonal closing times.
quote: Adult (13+): $34.95 online / $39.95 walk-up ... Child (3-12): $29.95 online / $34.95 walk-up ... Children under 3: Free ... opens 'daily at 9 a.m.' with closing times that 'vary by season.'

claim: Birch Aquarium added 2026 nighttime programming including the Meditation Ocean: Aquarius Reef Base exhibition debuting at an Oceans at Night event January 29, 2026, and Sunday-evening all-ages Birch After Hours from February 15, 2026.
quote: Meditation Ocean: Aquarius Reef Base ... featured during an Oceans at Night event starting January 29, 2026 ... Birch After Hours ... beginning February 15, 2026 ... Sunday nights from 5 to 7 p.m.

claim: Maritime Museum of San Diego general admission is $28 adult / $20 military & senior (62+) / $15 youth (6-17), free under 6, open daily 10 a.m.-5 p.m. with all-day access to historic ships including the 1863 Star of India.
quote: Adults: $28 ... Military & Senior (62+): $20 ... Youth (6-17): $15 ... Ages 5 & under: Free ... Open daily from 10 AM to 5 PM ... access to the museum's historic ships and exhibits

claim: Maritime Museum add-on tours include a 45-minute narrated Historic Bay Cruise for $10 and a 75-minute Naval History Bay Tour aboard PCF 816 Swift Boat for $15.
quote: A 45-minute narrated Historic Bay Cruise can be added for $10.00 ... A 75-minute narrated Naval History Bay Tour aboard the historic restored US Naval PCF 816 Swift Boat costs $15.00

claim: The New Children's Museum (downtown San Diego) charges $14 admission for ages 1-64, $10 for seniors 65+, free under 1, open Mon and Wed-Sun 9 a.m.-4 p.m. (closed Tuesday), with hands-on art installations like Teatro Pinata, Whammock! and Artopia studios.
quote: Admission is $14 for everyone between the ages of 1 and 64, $10 for seniors age 65 and older, and free for infants under the age of 1 ... open Monday 9am-4pm, closed Tuesday ... Teatro Piñata ... Whammock! ... Artopia: NCM Creative Studios

claim: The Carlsbad Flower Fields are open seasonally (roughly March through mid-May), 9am-6pm daily at 5704 Paseo del Norte, with peak ranunculus bloom late March through April; tickets must be bought online in advance.
quote: Peak ranunculus bloom occurs in late March through April... Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. daily (Entrance gate closes at 5:30 p.m.)... All tickets must be purchased before arrival

claim: The Carlsbad Flower Fields run March through May only, with ranunculus peaking late March through April, about 30 miles / 30 minutes north of downtown San Diego.
quote: The Flower Fields operate March-May exclusively. The peak blooming of the ranunculus is in late March through April.

claim: From San Diego, Temecula wine country is about 60 miles (under an hour), and Julian is roughly 90 minutes away at 4,225 feet elevation, known for apples and apple pie with fall apple season Sep-Nov.
quote: Julian is a small town in the mountains about 90 minutes from San Diego, famous for exactly one thing: apples and apple pie. The town sits at 4,225 feet elevation

claim: Temecula Valley has over 40 wineries spread along three wine trails (Rancho California Road, Calle Contento, De Portola Road), about 45-60 minutes north of San Diego, with Old Town tastings typically 4-6 wines for $10-20.
quote: Temecula Valley boasts dozens of wineries along three wine trails - Rancho California Road, Calle Contento and De Portola Road... Most tastings in Old Town Temecula include 4-6 wines for $10-20 per person

claim: MTS Route 992 stops at both airport terminals and reaches downtown's Santa Fe Depot in about 15 minutes for a $2.50 one-way fare, running every 15 minutes seven days a week, connecting to three Trolley lines, Rapid buses, COASTER and Amtrak.
quote: Route 992 stops on the elevated platform at both terminals and takes only 15 minutes to get to/from Santa Fe Depot... every 15 minutes for most of the day, 7 days a week. One-way fares are just $2.50

claim: The San Diego Flyer is a free electric shuttle connecting the airport to the Old Town Transit Center seven days a week, where travelers transfer to the Trolley, MTS buses, COASTER and Amtrak.
quote: The San Diego Flyer is a free electric shuttle-bus service that connects the airport to regional transit and operates seven days a week between the airport and the Old Town Transit Center

claim: Downtown San Diego is highly walkable, with the Gaslamp Quarter offering lodging, dining, shopping and entertainment within a single square mile, letting many visitors get around without a car.
quote: Downtown San Diego is an incredibly walkable area, and many visitors are able to enjoy the city without ever getting in a car!

claim: September and October are the best months to visit San Diego (warm 70s, swimmable ocean, thinner crowds, lower rates); May/June bring May Gray and June Gloom marine-layer overcast, and July-August are peak crowds with Comic-Con week selling out downtown hotels.
quote: May Gray and June Gloom bring overcast coastal skies from mid-May through June, though clouds typically clear by afternoon... July and August peak with crowds and premium pricing

claim: The best times to visit San Diego are March-May and September-November, with overcast May Gray and June Gloom days common as a marine layer blankets the coast and usually burns off by early afternoon.
quote: During May and June, overcast days occur often, so much so that locals designate the months as May Gray and June Gloom... The clouds usually burn off by early afternoon

claim: A car-free Tijuana day trip is easy via the MTS Blue Line Trolley from downtown's Santa Fe Depot to the San Ysidro border (about 40-50 minutes, ~17 miles), a short walk to the PedEast/PedWest pedestrian crossings.
quote: the easiest way to cross to Tijuana from San Diego is usually via the San Diego trolley, starting at downtown's Santa Fe Depot and hopping on the Blue Line straight to the San Ysidro border station. The trolley trip from downtown San Diego to the border takes about 40-50 minutes.

claim: As of 2025 the PedWest (El Chaparral) pedestrian crossing runs limited hours and is closed for entry into Mexico, so day-trippers should use the main PedEast crossing at the San Ysidro Port of Entry near the trolley station.
quote: As of September 2025, PedWest is open for limited hours in each direction during the day... PedWest is closed going into Mexico and only open from 6:00 to 14:00 each day going back to the U.S.

claim: A sensible first-timer 3-day San Diego itinerary devotes one day to Balboa Park/Zoo, one to La Jolla and the coast, and one to Coronado plus the harbor or Old Town, basing downtown or Little Italy; a car adds flexibility between neighborhoods.
quote: one day around Balboa Park, one day around La Jolla and the coast, and one final day around Coronado, the harbor, or Old Town... For a first trip, the easiest base is usually Downtown, Little Italy, or near the harbor.
